ms.report:
A) Public GitHub repository (project) is now live and public with the mentioned artifacts. It addresses the Acceptance Criteria A. For evidence, see https://github.com/KERIAuth/keriauth-blazor-wasm
B) Results of reviewing and testing the code in https://github.com/WebOfTrust/signify-browser-extension 
As part of our Fund 11 Milestone Report, we recorded a video that shows the signify-browser-extension and its dependency signify-ts, both being built and tested: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C8-wIn0Ul8-oG4ioN2NCWyGHK85tR7Ue/view?usp=sharing 
The signify-ts project at https://github.com/weboftrust/signify-ts has automated tests implemented and run via GitHub actions, which can be seen at https://github.com/WebOfTrust/signify-ts/actions with results https://github.com/WebOfTrust/signify-ts/actions/workflows/main.yml. We also included text output from our local running of the signify-ts build, unit tests, and integration tests, which can be found referenced in our following GitHub issue: https://github.com/KERIAuth/keriauth-blazor-wasm/issues/16 and at https://github.com/KERIAuth/keriauth-blazor-wasm/files/15448087/signify-ts.results.of.build.unit.test.and.integration.test.run.2024-05-26.txt.
The primary dependency the signify-browser-extension and this project’s keriauth-blazor-wasm code each have is the signify-ts library, which both we’ll also use to communicate with a KERIA agent service developed and maintained by the WebOfTrust community.
We also reviewed the code of signify-browser-extension. The code is under active development, and we continue to monitor commits to it in GitHub, as well as attend weekly meetings with the developers as part of the WebOfTrust implementer’s call. 
We found the code’s good use of ECMAScript Modules modules and React resulted in clean code. Those choices may be easier to work with than the C# Blazor WASM design approach we have chosen. We stuck with C# Blazor WASM because of our familiarity with it and potential to leverage the co

ms.promise:
A) Coded protocol(s) in Typescript (delivered as JavaScript) API between a verifying website and the extension.
B) Created (or used existing sample of) a verifying website.
C) Third-party KERI component source can issue a credential (in ACDC format) to extension holder.
D) Extension User can authorize with website with KERI AID and cryptographic signing.

G) Supporting source code and artifacts in repo.
H) The project team has conducted one or more conversations with Cardano blockchain projects to better understand their problems and how this KERI extension solution concept may address their needs. That conversation is documented.

ms.report:
Outputs (with evidence of Milestone Completion comments)
A) Coded protocol(s) in Typescript (delivered as JavaScript) API between a verifying website and the extension.
・Done. The Typescript source for this API defines typescript interfaces for the messages and responses communicated between a web page and the extension’s content script. These are further described on the project’s README.md and Messages Page.

B) Created (or used existing sample of) a verifying website.
・Done. For our integration testing, we are leveraging the “reg-pilot” website project https://github.com/GLEIF-IT/reg-pilot-webapp which is described in its full context here: https://github.com/GLEIF-IT/reg-pilot 
・This is completed as demonstrated in the video (link toward the end of this report).

C) Third-party KERI component source can issue a credential (in ACDC format) to extension holder.
・Done. For the Milestone 3 deliverable, we used a reg-pilot-webapp hosted by Roots-ID here: https://reg-pilot-webapp-test.rootsid.cloud/. They populated it with test credentials via scripts similar to those in signify-ts, here: https://github.com/WebOfTrust/signify-ts/blob/main/examples/integration-scripts/credentials.test.ts, as was demonstrated in our Milestone 1 report. (reference that. Also include screenshots from M1 report, and screenshots of credentials in M3.)

D) Extension User can authorize with website with KERI AID and cryptographic signing.
・Done. This is completed as is demonstrated in the video, integrating with the website https://cardano-watcher.rootsid.cloud/

E) Extension User can authenticate with website. Note, in this proof-of concept, the website might not completely verify and validate the presented credential, although that is the stretch-goal.
・Done. This is essentially completed as demonstrated in the video, showing an integration with https://reg-pilot-webapp-dev.rootsid.cloud/. More complete validation of the credential is under development within the KERI community.
